panels.title: Download throughput
panels.description: Article bytes received from all backends.

panels.title: Missing (430) share
panels.description: 430 replies divided by all backend commands. A 430 on one backend is normal; this is how often lookups miss.

panels.title: Missing (430) share by backend
panels.description: Share of commands answered 430. A backend that suddenly misses much more than usual may have lost retention or be routing to a bad server.

panels.title: Article standing by backend
panels.description: Falls by 1/8 on every 430 and climbs by 1/128 of the gap on every hit. With routing.article.standing = "adaptive" it scales the backend's share of article lookups within its tier, so a backend hit by a takedown drops to the bottom and works its way back. A backend near 0 while its tier peers stay near 1 is missing that download.

panels.title: Refusals and server errors by backend
Transport errors by backend
panels.description: Connection-level failures (resets, timeouts, TLS errors): all backend errors minus 4xx/5xx replies.

panels.title: Time to first byte p50 / p95
panels.description: Only measured for commands timed individually (retries, failovers, prechecks).

panels.title: Exchange duration p95
panels.description: How long one exchange held a backend connection.

panels.title: Connection attempts by outcome
panels.description: login_refused usually means the provider account's connection limit is reached.

panels.title: Connection cap
panels.description: Connections each backend may hold. With connection_cap = "adaptive" it drops to the accepted count on a refused login and climbs back one a minute, and past max_connections one every 10 minutes while saturated.

panels.title: Backlog skips and busy timeouts
panels.description: Requests that passed over a backend because its queue was too long, or waited and gave up.

panels.title: Delivery rate per connection
panels.description: Article bytes per busy second per connection, client stalls excluded. The short horizon follows the current download; compare backends to see who is actually fast for this release.

panels.title: First-byte time (EWMA)
panels.description: Time from sending an article command to its first response. Close to the whole exchange time means the backend is waiting on its server (pipelining could help); a small share means it is bandwidth-bound.

panels.title: Leased idle connections
panels.description: Connections a client holds between its commands without an exchange running. High while requests wait elsewhere means capacity is reserved, not working.

panels.title: Client stall
panels.description: Seconds per second article writes spent blocked on a slow client (1.0 = one connection's worth of time held by the client).

panels.title: Client bytes
panels.description: Updated when client sessions end; use backend article bytes for live throughput.
